messages:
maya: Customer reported streaming responses cutting off mid-token and immediate reconnect loop (~13s). Partial final chunks, then server FIN. They also saw a billing spike (2x) during the window.

alex: Which endpoint + auth? Can you paste logs and a minimal curl repro (non-prod) so we can reproduce quickly?

maya: Endpoint is /v1/streams/generate (hosted). Token is customer-managed. Minimal repro I used locally:
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"test backpressure"}' \\
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate\"
```
Client is an iOS SDK instance that suspends reads when backgrounded. Headers are chunked transfer + SSE.

maya: Server-side logs from our east proxy (sanitized):
```text
[proxy] 2026-03-12T14:05:22.123Z writev: EAGAIN, wrote=0
[proxy] 2026-03-12T14:05:22.123Z aborting connection id=aa3f, reason=slow_consumer
[ingress] 2026-03-12T14:05:22.124Z upstream closed with partial payload len=84
```

ryan: That looks like socket send buffer filled -> writev EAGAIN -> proxy triggers abort path. Are they behind corp proxy / nginx sidecar? @jess can you confirm cluster config?

jess: Yes, flow goes through east-us proxy cluster that has an nginx sidecar with proxy_buffering enabled. I've seen sbuff overflows when mobile clients pause reads for >10s. Can you confirm client read behavior (pause durations)?

maya: Mobile client often pauses reads when the app goes to background; I've observed pauses of 10-30s. Reconnects align with put/background toggles.

alex: Hypothesis: slow consumer (client pauses) -> kernel send buffer fills -> writev returns EAGAIN -> proxy kills connection to avoid queuing memory -> client reconnects and stream is restarted, final chunk lost -> duplicates/reconnects cause billing count to spike. Makes sense? :thinking:

ryan: Yep. Mitigation buckets:
- Proxy: loosen abort threshold (allow larger sendq) or increase slow_consumer timeout; or implement smarter backpressure stall tracking per-connection.
- Runtime: emit resumable stream ids/sequence so clients can request missing tokens on reconnect.
- Client: smaller chunk sizes / keepalive pings / avoid background-suspend reads where possible.

jess: Quick/urgent patch: I can increase proxy send buffer to 1MB and bump slow_consumer timeout from 5s to 30s on east-us cluster as a canary. Rolling to 5% now.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: proxy-config v2.11 -> 5% nodes

maya: Customer wants an immediate workaround they can apply on their end while we patch. Any recommended client changes?

alex: Ask them to enable TCP keepalives on iOS (set SO_KEEPALIVE with a shorter interval) and increase the socket recv timeout to 60s. Recommend using NSURLSession in foreground mode for critical streams or implement last-event-id style resume. Also advise smaller chunk sizes from our runtime if possible.

maya: Sent guidance to customer. They also asked for billing credits for the partial outputs. Can billing review?

ryan: @billing-team can you review usage for acct-432 between 2026-03-12T14:00 and 2026-03-12T14:20? Expect duplicated tokens due to reconnects.

sre-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-148 opened. Assigned: @ryan @jess

jess: Canary metrics so far: EAGAIN logs dropped by ~70% on 5% canary nodes. No new regressions. Proceeding to 30% and monitoring sendq_drops metric.

alex: Action items (short):
- jess: finish proxy config rollout + add sendq_drops metric and alert
- alex: add regression test simulating paused-read (sleep 15s) client and assert proxy does not abort
- billing: review credits request for acct-432 window
- maya: communicate interim guidance and follow up with customer

maya: ack, will update customer after billing reply + canary progression :thumbsup:

ryan: Also long-term: add resume tokens to streaming protocol or server-side prefix caching so resumed clients can request missing suffixes (prevents data loss + billing duplication). Filing RFC separately.

maya: thanks everyone, closing loop later.
